author: Linda Cook
title: Grow Clinton assists with regional workforce response to Tyson Foods, Joslin, closure - NewsBreak
text:
By Linda Cook ,
6 hours ago
The recent closure of the Tyson Foods plant in Joslin, Illinois, has resulted in about 2,500 workers losing their jobs, creating a significant impact on the regional workforce and surrounding
communities, a news release from Grow Clinton says.
Grow Clinton is working closely with the Eastern Iowa Workforce Board (EIWB) and regional partners to support individuals and families affected by the closure. Director of Workforce Development & Talent Attraction for Grow Clinton, Stacy Borgeson serves as member of the EIWB. Efforts are underway to assist those who have been displaced.
These efforts include informational meetings, hiring events, and connections to workforce development and support services throughout the region.
“Events of this magnitude have a tremendous impact on workers, families, employers, and communities across our region,” said Borgeson. “Our regional partners are committed to making sure impacted workers have access to the resources, information, and employment opportunities they need as they navigate this transition.”
Grow Clinton is also encouraging employers with significant hiring needs to participate in the regional response. Organizations interested in hiring impacted workers or becoming involved in upcoming workforce efforts should contact Stacy Borgeson, director of workforce development and talent attraction, Grow Clinton, here .
